the evidence for a routine adolescent meningococcal vaccine program in Canada is strong.
a vaccination strategy targeting adolescents is feasible, and may have a significant impact on meningococcal epidemiology.
the indirect effects of adolescent vaccination may be large and long lasting, and that the cost-effectiveness of this strategy may be better than other approaches.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adolescent immunization strategies should be considered for all vaccine-preventable diseases.
vaccination of adolescents against meningococci is a promising strategy to control disease in the short and long term.
adolescent vaccination is a potentially powerful tool for controlling meningococcal transmission and disease, but the optimal timing, vaccine type, and vaccination strategies remain uncertain.
